title: Count the ranges
prompt: This program makes a few DataFrames with `spark.range` and counts their rows. What does it print? Type each line on its own line.
hints: `spark.range` works like Python's `range`: it starts at 0 by default and leaves out the end.
`spark.range(0, 10, 3)` goes up in steps of 3 and stops before 10. List the numbers.
Every range has the same single column.
explanation: `spark.range(10)` holds 0 to 9, which is 10 rows, and `spark.range(3, 10)` holds 3 to 9, which is 7. Stepping by 3 from 0 gives 0, 3, 6 and 9: 4 rows. The only column is `id`, so `columns` is `['id']`.
